title: adaptive-memory-telemetry-predicted-eviction-and-granular-staging
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduces a telemetry-driven eviction predictor and a tenant-prioritized staging layer for KV cache to reduce fragmentation and spillover; improves tail latency under mixed workloads.
description:
Context and motivation:
We have recurring tail-latency regressions in multi-tenant KV workloads caused by fragment churn and large spill events when tenant working sets spike. Current eviction is size/time heuristics that do not leverage richer telemetry (access histograms, kernel hotness signals, contiguous-span scores). This PR adds a lightweight telemetry-driven eviction predictor and a granular staging area that temporarily demotes objects according to predicted reuse and fragmentation footprint, reducing unnecessary spillover to disk and improving latency stability across tenants.

High-level design:
- Telemetry pipeline: gather per-tenant access histograms (bucketed by recency/sequence-length), contiguous-span fragmentation score, and kernel-selection hints emitted by the scheduler into an in-memory ring buffer.
- Eviction predictor: a compact model (decision tree rules encoded in C++) that combines telemetry to produce an eviction score per entry. Predictor runs incrementally on eviction candidates to avoid global scans.
- Granular staging layer: small in-memory staging queues (per-tenant, per-shard) that hold demoted items for a short TTL before spilling. Staging keeps contiguous segments together where possible to allow compaction/coalescing and reduces IO amplification.
- Tenant-prioritized spill partitioning: when spill is unavoidable, the spill partitioner uses tenant SLAs and predictor confidence to split large spill batches into prioritized chunks, allowing high-priority tenants to remain in memory.
- Backpressure hooks: predictor confidence and staging occupancy feed into request scheduling/batching so the runtime can throttle low-priority background jobs and favor interactive token paths.

Commits (summary):
- commit 1: add telemetry ring buffer and histogram collector (src/kv/telemetry/*)
- commit 2: implement eviction predictor and unit tests (src/kv/evictor/predictor.{cc,h})
- commit 3: introduce staging queues and TTL eviction policy (src/kv/staging/*)
- commit 4: spill partitioner and tenant-priority policy (src/kv/spill/partitioner.{cc,h})
- commit 5: integrate backpressure hooks with scheduler and add e2e perf test harness changes (tests/perf/kv_telemetry_smoke.sh)

Files changed (high-level):
- src/kv/telemetry/collector.cc - new: ring buffer + lightweight histogram API
- src/kv/evictor/predictor.cc - new: rule-table-based predictor with feature normalization
- src/kv/staging/queue.cc - new: per-tenant staging queues and compaction trigger
- src/kv/spill/partitioner.cc - updated: spill batching refactor to support prioritized partitions
- src/serving/scheduler/backpressure.cc - updated: hooks to slow background workloads based on staging occupancy
- tests/unit/evictor_predictor_test.cc - new: coverage for predictor edge cases
- tests/perf/kv_telemetry_smoke.sh - new: lightweight workload to reproduce previous spill bursts

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: predictor rule coverage and staging TTL behavior.
- Integration: local KV perf harness reports 18-32% reduction in 99th percentile latency across mixed-tenancy replay compared to baseline for the workloads we used.
- CI matrix: linux/amd64 build + unit tests + perf smoke. First CI run failed on a flaky timing assertion in staging queue tests; I fixed the test to use a simulated clock and retriggered. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Review conversation (highlights - condensed):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end; can we keep the predictor model pluggable?"
- Author (Maya): "Yes — core predictor is rule-based and loaded via a small registry; follow-up will add a JS/Bento config loader. Kept API small to minimize hot path overhead."
- Priya Patel (reviewer): "Staging queues look promising, but what about memory accounting?"
- Author: "Staging per-tenant caps are enforced via token buckets and reflected in the global mempool metrics. Added explicit accounting metrics: kv.staging_bytes, kv.staging_entries, kv.staging_pressure."
- Diego Ramos (reviewer): "We should be careful with the spill partitioner ordering to avoid starvation."
- Author: "Partitioner uses a weighted-round-robin across priority buckets with a max-slice limit; documented behavior in code comments and added unit tests to prevent starvation regressions."
- QA: requested a perf run across GC-heavy nodes. I ran the job and included the artifacts in the PR comment (link omitted in this JSON).

Performance notes and rationale:
- Predictor avoids full-table scans by operating on eviction candidates discovered by the existing LRU sampler; cost measured at ~0.5 us per candidate on our benchmark, negligible compared to IO.
- Staging TTL default is 5s with an exponential backoff multiplier for re-demotion; tuned after several replay runs to balance compaction opportunity vs. memory pressure.
- Observed improvements primarily in reducing large contiguous spill events and downstream IO contention; average token-serving latency unchanged, but 99th and 99.9th latency improved for multi-tenant bursts.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature gate controlled via runtime flags (kv.telemetry_evictor_enabled, kv.staging_ttl_ms, kv.spill_partitioning_enabled). Default: disabled on stable main.
- Rollout plan: enable in canary, monitor kv.staging_pressure and kv.evictions_by_tenant metrics, then incrementally enable across low-risk regions before global rollout.

Operational and observability additions:
- New metrics: kv.telemetry_samples_total, kv.eviction_predictor_confidence{bucket}, kv.staging_bytes, kv.spill_partitions_emitted
- New logs: structured events when partitioner preempts a spill batch for a high-priority tenant (severity INFO)
- Dashboards: added a perf dashboard tile for staging occupancy and predictor hit/miss rates.

Follow-ups (planned):
- Expose predictor tuning knobs in Console for experimental rollouts.
- Add a small BPF sampling path to enrich kernel hotness signals if kernel-level hints are enabled.
- Consider a learned predictor fallback (ML model) if rule-set coverage proves insufficient for some tenant patterns.

Merge outcome:
- After addressing test timing flakiness and adding the memory-accounting metrics requested by Priya, reviewers approved. PR was squashed and merged into main on 2026-03-01.

Notes for reviewers/handoff:
- See README at src/kv/telemetry/README.md for configuration examples and suggested alert thresholds.
- There is a small perf harness under tests/perf that can be used to reproduce the 99th percentile improvements documented in the perf artifacts.

Links (internal):
- Linear: ENG-3421 (telemetry-driven eviction), ENG-3478 (tenant spill priority)
- Perf artifacts: [see CI artifacts]

This PR aims to reduce the impact of fragmentation-driven spillovers without changing the fundamental eviction semantics. It prefers a conservative, observable rollout with operator controls and follow-up plans for richer telemetry integration.
